children: Italian luxury group Armani could bring in more than one investor as it prepares to sell a 15% stake in accordance with founder Giorgio Armani’s will, CEO Giuseppe Marsocci said Sunday.
Marsocci said the company is not required to sell the entire stake to a single buyer and could divide it among several investors. He stressed that no final decision has been made, Reuters reported.

Giorgio Armani, who died at age 91 in September 2025, directed that an initial 15% stake be sold within 12 to 18 months of his death. His succession plan calls for a larger stake sale or a potential stock-market listing afterward.

For investors, the process could reshape ownership of one of the world’s largest remaining independent luxury houses while creating an opportunity for major European consumer companies to gain exposure to the Armani brand. A consortium could also reduce the financial commitment and strategic risk for any single buyer. The eventual valuation and ownership structure could have implications for publicly traded companies involved in the process.

Marsocci, who became CEO last October, declined to say whether Armani had received interest from parties beyond those named by its founder. He said the company plans to follow the timetable laid out in the will, though any deal will depend on agreement over valuation and other terms.

The Financial Times reported Sunday that Armani is preparing for discussions with LVMH, L’Oreal and EssilorLuxottica in the coming weeks. One possibility raised informally would have the three companies jointly acquire the 15% stake.
Reuters previously reported that EssilorLuxottica could consider teaming up with other bidders.

The ownership transition comes as Armani also makes changes to its creative leadership. The company this month appointed former Versace designer Dario Vitale as creative director of Emporio Armani and Giorgio Armani accessories.

Marsocci characterized the appointment as part of an effort to preserve the founder’s design legacy while positioning the company for future growth. He identified accessories as a particularly promising area for expansion.

title: Armani open to multiple investors for planned 15% stake
